faq: Will I keep my search rankings after the move?

Nobody can promise that. Redirects and matching page content give you the best chance of keeping traffic, and we check for the common mistakes. Some temporary movement after a platform change is normal.
Can every platform handle the redirects?
Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce and Wix all support them, with different limits on size and rules. We choose the method that fits, and tell you early if your plan caps the number of redirects.
What if the domain name changes too?
Then redirects also need to work across domains, and we need access to both. We map the old domain to the new one and test it. Tell us in the order form so we scope it properly.
Do you need access to my Google Search Console?
It helps a lot because it shows which pages already bring visitors. Access is optional and view-only is enough. Without it we rely on a crawl and any analytics export you can share.

desc:
301 redirects and URL mapping for migrations send every old web address to its matching page on your new store. Ecom Swift LLC crawls your current site, maps the links and tests the redirects, so shoppers and search engines still find you.

## What are 301 redirects and URL mapping?

A 301 redirect is an instruction that says a page has moved permanently and tells browsers and search engines where it lives now. URL mapping is the list that pairs each old address with its new one. Together they make sure an old link in Google, an email, a social post or a bookmark opens a real page instead of an error.

Every platform builds addresses in its own pattern. A product that lived under one path on the old store will sit under a different path on the new one, even when the name is identical.

## Why old links break when a store moves

Search engines have stored thousands of your addresses. When a page disappears, the visitor sees a not-found message and the search engine slowly drops the page. Years of link value built up by blogs, press and customers can be lost.

Your own marketing is at risk too. Old emails, printed material, ads and social profiles keep pointing at addresses that no longer exist. Each broken link is a shopper who left without seeing a product.

## How redirects protect traffic and sales

Redirects pass visitors, and much of the page's standing in search, to the new address. A shopper who clicks a saved link lands on the right product and can buy. Search engines learn the new address and keep showing it.

Results still depend on factors outside our control, such as how much the content and structure change and how quickly search engines revisit the site. What redirects do is remove the avoidable loss. Without them, nothing connects the old store to the new one.

## What a thorough redirect project includes

- A crawl of your current site to list every live address.
- Data on which pages actually get visits, so the important ones are mapped first.
- A match for each product, collection, blog post and page.
- Rules for patterns, such as every address under a tag path, in larger catalogs.
- Handling of address variations with filters or query strings.
- A decision for pages with no match, such as sending them to the nearest category.
- A check for loops and long chains, which slow visitors and confuse search engines.
- Bulk testing of every redirect after it is set up.
- A review of image and file links.
- A spreadsheet showing where each old link now leads.

## What we do

We crawl the old store and combine that list with your search and traffic data where you can share it. We then match each address to the best page on the new store, using product names, handles and content. Where no page fits, we choose the closest useful destination rather than the home page.

Redirects are added in the new store's own redirect tool, or in the host's settings where the platform needs it. We test them in bulk and send you a report of any that fail. Larger packages cover more addresses, pattern rules, filter links and a recheck of errors a week after launch.

Where the domain also changes, the map includes the new domain so nothing is left behind.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep the old store crawlable until the map is finished.
- Prioritize pages that bring search visitors.
- Submit the new sitemap to search engines after launch.
- Review error reports in the first weeks.
- Keep product names consistent where you can.

**Avoid:**
- Redirecting every old page to the home page.
- Building long chains of redirects.
- Using temporary redirects for permanent moves.
- Deleting the map after launch.
- Changing page addresses again right after the move.

## Who this is for

An owner with a store that gets steady visitors from Google and cannot lose them. A blogger-turned-seller with hundreds of articles linked from other sites. A brand changing both platform and domain at once.

## What we need from you

Give us the old store address and, if you can, view access to your search console and analytics, plus a list of pages you know matter. We never need passwords. A collaborator or read-only user is enough for the crawl and checks.
